text:
Maya: Heads up quick sync on GA acceptance edge cases we didn't fully cover: SLA exceptions (force majeure/data center failures), data residency impact on monitoring surface, and cross-customer credit math for partial outages. Need owners + wording by EOD.
Ravi: I'll take SLA exceptions. Draft: "SLA does not apply during force majeure events, scheduled maintenance windows, or customer-side network issues." Want legal to weigh in on "customer-side" definition.
legal-bot: Noted. Legal suggests adding: "Customer-side incidents = configuration errors, compromised credentials, or network interruptions not caused by Redwood." Will provide canonical clause.
Sana: Monitoring owner here. Data residency note: Private/VPC customers may opt out of route-level telemetry. If opted out, Console will show aggregate metrics only and those customers are excluded from per-route SLO calculations. Need to reflect in SLA doc.
Ellen: Ops/SRE: For cross-customer partial outages (e.g., 30% of routing cluster), recommend per-customer impact assessment before any credit. We should avoid blanket credits when only a subset affected. Propose tagging impacted customers via telemetry and generating a validation report.
Tomas: Product question: do we want to promise region-level vs global-level SLAs? Some customers will expect multi-region guarantees. My preference: GA only guarantees per-region SLOs for Reserved/Dedicated with active multi-region config. Add that to doc.
Maya: Good call. Make a short bullet: "Global SLA requires explicit multi-region deployment and a supporting runbook." Tomas, add sample wording.
Ravi: For credit math: propose simple and conservative formula: credit = min(50%, (affected_request_count / total_request_count) * monthly_subscription). Example in doc. Finance to confirm cap.
finance-bot: Finance note: Cap credits at 50% of monthly recurring charges; one-time overage refunds handled separately. Will confirm rounding rules.
legal-bot: Also add a dispute window: customers must submit SLA credit claims within 30 days of incident end with supporting logs. We'll add process link.
Sana: Important to state telemetry fallback: if customer opts out of route telemetry, we may use synthetic canary data plus customer-provided logs to validate incidents. Add that to runbook.
Ellen: Add operational rule: if rollback or mitigation causes reduced quality (fallback to lower-quality model), we do not count that as SLA failure if fallback was enabled by customer or triggered automatically per policy. Must mark requests with fallback=true for audit.
Tomas: Docs side: I'll add two short examples: 1) Regional outage affecting 20% of customers -> sample credit flow. 2) Customer opt-out of telemetry -> how we validate. Priya (docs) not in thread but will coordinate visuals.
Maya: Action list: Ravi -> SLA exceptions + sample clauses (12h). Legal -> canonical "customer-side" + dispute window (12h). Sana -> telemetry/residency note + validation fallback (12h). Ellen -> tagging/ops validation process + runbook snippet (12h). Finance -> confirm credit cap and rounding (12h).
Maya: I'll stitch into a single customer-facing section and circulate for acceptance. If anyone expects delays, flag here. :thumbsup:
